title: Is the sum of a number and its reverse always divisible by 11?
description: A two digit number is added to its reverse instead of subtracted. Letters show the sum is eleven times the sum of the digits, so eleven always divides it, and thirty one checks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding the number and its reverse gives eleven of each digit, so the sum is eleven times the digit total. Watch for students who test three examples and stop without using letters.

video_script.why: The child reuses the letters for a number and its reverse, adds instead of subtracting, and sees eleven appear.
video_script.substitution: Add 10a + b and 10b + a, group the letters to get 11a + 11b, take out 11, and check with 31 and 13.
video_script.anchor: the pairs 31 and 13, 28 and 82, 12 and 21 added on the board
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, eleven always divides the sum, because it is eleven times the sum of the digits

final_answer.spoken: eleven times the sum of the digits

maths_rules: 11a + 11b = 11 × (a + b), so the sum is divisible by 11
video_script.design: One idea: the sum of a number and its reverse is eleven times the sum of its digits. The three examples stay on the board and the check is the last step.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book. It changes the trick, and adds the number and its reverse.
<bookmark mark='examples'/>Thirty one plus thirteen is forty four. Twenty eight plus eighty two is one hundred ten. Twelve plus twenty one is thirty three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Eleven divides every one of these, but is this always true, and can algebra show it?

beats.on_screen: the additions stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.plan: the number and its reverse are written with letters

narration: <bookmark mark='plan'/>We use the same letters as in the trick. The number is ten times eigh plus bee, and the reverse is ten times bee plus eigh.

beats.on_screen: Given: a two digit number with tens digit a and ones digit b, added to its reverse

marks.given: the number and its digits are written with letters

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a two digit number with eigh in the tens place and bee in the ones place. We add it to its reverse.

beats.on_screen: To show: the sum is always divisible by 11

marks.find: the aim is written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to show that eleven always divides the sum.

marks.group: the a terms and the b terms are grouped

beats.colours: the a terms and the b terms in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, add the number and its reverse.
<bookmark mark='group'/>Group the eighs together and group the bees together.
<bookmark mark='elevens'/>Ten eigh plus eigh is eleven eigh, and bee plus ten bee is eleven bee.

marks.common: the common 11 is pulled out in front
marks.div: the words 11 divides it are written

beats.colours: the common 11 in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='common'/>Step two, take out eleven, because both parts have eleven. That leaves eleven times eigh plus bee.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Eleven is a factor of the sum, so eleven divides it.

marks.digits: 3 + 1 = 4 is written beside it and the two 4s are matched

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step three, check with thirty one. Forty four divided by eleven is four.
<bookmark mark='digits'/>Three plus one is also four, so the two match.

marks.ans: the answer sum = 11 × (a + b) is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Yes, eleven always divides the sum, because it is eleven times the sum of the digits.
